title: Startups can get up to ₹25 crore to develop technology: iDEX funds drones, robots and AI projects; check el...
summary: iDEX launches grants up to 25 crore rupees for tech startups developing drones and AI
detailed: The government's iDEX initiative helps startups build drones, robots, or software that can be used by the armed forces.
Startups working on drones, robotics, cyber security, surveillance equipment, AI, and modern communication technology can apply.
ADITI scheme: The grant ceiling is up to ₹25 crore for selected defence technologies.
If the idea matches an iDEX challenge and is selected, it can receive a grant to build and test the drone prototype.
sentences: The government's iDEX initiative helps startups build drones, robots, or software that can be used by the armed forces.
As of February 2026, 676 startups, MSMEs, and innovators had joined it, and 548 development contracts had been signed.
58 prototypes were approved, with a potential procurement value of about ₹3,853 crore.
What kinds of ideas get support?
Startups working on drones, robotics, cyber security, surveillance equipment, AI, and modern communication technology can apply.
The idea should be linked to a need of the armed forces and offer a practical solution to a problem.
General challenge: A grant of up to ₹1.5 crore per project.
ADITI scheme: The grant ceiling is up to ₹25 crore for selected defence technologies.
Not every startup gets the maximum amount.
The sum is decided on the basis of the project's needs, its budget, and approval.
Payment is made on completion of the work.
DPIIT-recognised startups, Indian MSMEs, and individual innovators can apply.
Individual innovators must set up a startup before signing the grant agreement.
This support is given not merely for starting a business, but for developing a technical solution to a problem in the defence sector.
Different challenges are issued under iDEX from time to time.
Each challenge has its own application deadline and conditions.
Before applying, be sure to check the available challenges and their timelines on the official website.
Understand with an example Suppose a startup wants to build a drone that can watch enemy activity from a distance.
It has an early model of the drone, but needs funds to improve it according to the army's requirements and to test it.
If the idea matches an iDEX challenge and is selected, it can receive a grant to build and test the drone prototype.
What will you get if selected?
The startup may get a grant to build the prototype, expert advice, and testing facilities as required.
The money is released when the set targets are met.
Once the product is ready, the army decides on buying it according to its own needs and the prescribed process.
Getting funding does not mean getting an order to buy the product.
Select the challenge related to your technology.
Fill in the idea, its usefulness, the project budget, and the technical details.
A team of experts examines the applications.
Those selected will be called for the next stage of the process.
